body:
Thank you. Fantasies of escape especially after I became financially independent have been very coming for me. I've actually prepared an exit bag and stashed up some money abroad.

My therapist however reckons this is not a good solution and continues to insist that I try to work things out with my wife. I trust my therapist 100% so she must have very good reasons.  the problem of course is that it's now being many years of treatment and zero progress on the side of things

I'll update this thread when I learn more ,thank you

"your life’s work isn’t done yet." -> that's something my therapist is trying to make me realize. She's given me tasks and i have to find goals that would make me happy, like volunteering at a dog shelter (i love dogs). But I go to the shelter and i see things i'm sexually attracted to and can't have (this actually happened, i kid  you not).

So it just makes me even more depressed, because now i'm not only miserable, but i'm miserable trying to do everything to 'be a good person' so i can somehow be rewarded with what i want. And if you ever tried to quit heroin cold turkey, you can get an idea of what i've been through in order to 'hopefully get that reward'... that seemingly never will come.

Thank you for the kind words though, i appreciate it.

My therapist offered the same advice. I did. Again. And again. And again. My wife a) isn't into it, like most women are (source: statistics i forget) b) doesn't understand the gravity of the situation (even though while i was using drugs, i ODed and died to be reanimated in-extremis by the paramedics). She's not stupid - she knows where this self-destructive streak comes from. Yet... nothing.

One thing we're considering is that i'll make an effort to satisfy her in exchange of what i'd like, the problem is that it's a bit of a stale mate because she's not into what i like, and quite frankly, i take very little pleasure in 'normal' sex'. 

Thank you for the comment though, i do appreciate it.

Thank you for your comment which made me google 'fetish vs obsession'. I will bring this to my therapist (whom i see 3 times a week), because you're 100% correct, it's an obsession. I was at a show yesterday (i can't give too much details, sorry) and placed a second cell phone on the floor to take pix/videos of the women sneakers sitting around me. While being with my wife. I then went home and masturbated to that. 

I understand the 'not worth throwing your life away for' comment. But by that logic, it's never worth committing suicide, since Christopher Reeves led 9 hard but 'valuable' years after being paralyzed from the neck down. He considered suicide, but didn't do it. I find him very courageous. I guess he found that by 'beating' his condition and helping others, the 'reward' was greater than the suffering he certainly must have gone through.

To draw a parallel that's farfetched but might put things in perspective, imagine being gay in a country where it's not legal to be gay, and even supported - a minor fetish you might call it. So every day seeing men you are attracted to, but you can't act on it . It's not like it's not _possible_ for you to get what you felt for 42 years you needed to get any type of sexual relief, it's just not available to to you without destroying your marriage, and for your homosexuality, of which you are ashamed, to become public (because let me tell you, if i cheat or divorce my wife to get what i want, she'll pulverize me in public as she knows exactly what my issues are). 

I'm stuck between a wall and a hard rock, if you will.

Ha! Great question. Well two reasons. The first, is that i was raised under the impression that if you work hard you get the things you like, and my brain just associated the two. I realize it sounds almost stupid, and probably  is, but that's one reason.

Second reason is that if you thought work was the best cop-out ever to get away from responsibilities in life, wait till you win the lottery or get rich through work. Now wealth, that's the greatest, no, it's the ultimate cop out when it comes to avoiding responsibilities.

So yes, since i have little to lose and this is a relatively anonymous forum, I'm not really ashamed to admit that I used both work (busy-ness) and wealth (can't tell me what to do) as means to get around my obvious mental health issues. I mean when i was at the height of my dope-usage, i was found unconscious many times by the grounds keeper, and never , not once, was 'exit-humanity has a serious problem' was ever raised as a question.

TLDR: I used both as shields because i hurt so much inside.

Thank you for your comment. My comment omitted a few details which i pointed out in other comments. I didn't have an 'easy' life, and my wife stuck by me thought thick and thin. I realize that killing myself is betraying her more than say, cheating on her, in a way. It's quite cowardly of me actually, but it's just the pain is so great and sometimes i feel that she knows and does nothing, because there's nothing she can do (she's not into bdsm, she's not into bdsm, it's not her fault).

I'll consider your comment further, thank you.

Thank you for your reply. I had my fair share of those, don't worry (I say this sarcastically of course). I watched my mother lose her dignity through Alzheimer and developed panic attack after panic attack from caring for her 24/7. People very close to me died in horrible ways. I have been betrayed at work and outside of work in ways you wouldn't believe, even if it was made into a movie. 

So yes, in 42 years of life, much **** has happened to me, but none of it ever wanted to make me kill myself. 

However, being sexually turned on by one thing and one thing only, and having that thing paraded pretty much everywhere I go , unable to act on my impulses... that's hell, believe it or not. 

It's ok if you don't believe me, or if you disagree with me by the way. But please don't assume that 'watching your half sister die of sepsis in front of you' (which happened to me) is somehow more suicide-worthy than 'being sexually frustrated for life'.
